statement: Extending New York City's school-zone speed cameras to 24-hour, 7-day operation on 1 August 2022 reduced injury crashes in the newly enforced hours (weekday 10 pm-6 am and weekends) relative to the weekday 6 am-10 pm hours that were already enforced.

graph_evidence.note: Abstract check: PMID 17666698 (Barcelona) reports RR 0.73 (0.63-0.85) for collisions on the beltway with cameras; the graph's second association from that paper (RR 0.99, 0.90-1.10, labelled 'people injured among the population affected by the speed cameras') is the comparison arterial roads without cameras, so it is mis-extracted. PMID 14693888 (South Wales, mobile cameras) reports injurious crash rate ratio 0.49 (0.42-0.57) within 500 m routes, with decreases in day and night.

literature.citation: Wilson C, Willis C, Hendrikz JK, Le Brocque R, Bellamy N (2010). Speed cameras for the prevention of road traffic injuries and deaths. Cochrane Database Syst Rev (10):CD004607.
literature.finding: Reductions in injury crashes near camera sites of roughly 8-49%, fatal and serious 11-44%.

literature.citation: NYC DOT (2023, 2025). Speed camera program reports and press releases.
literature.finding: About 7.6% fewer injuries in the new overnight and weekend hours at camera locations in the first year (agency figure).

prediction.magnitude: Citywide, because cameras cover a small share of street length, the ratio of ratios (injury crashes in new hours / old hours, Aug 2022-Jul 2023 vs Aug 2021-Jul 2022) between 0.92 and 1.00. Persons injured and pedestrians injured are secondary outcomes.
prediction.support_if: Ratio of ratios below 1 with a 95% interval below 1.
prediction.refute_if: Ratio of ratios at or above 1 with an interval that excludes 0.97.

plan: Data: NYPD Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (data.cityofnewyork.us h9gi-nx95), aggregated by SoQL to counts by month, day of week and hour. Exposure groups: new hours = Mon-Fri 22:00-05:59 and all Sat-Sun; old hours = Mon-Fri 06:00-21:59. Outcomes: crashes with >= 1 person injured or killed (primary), persons injured, pedestrians injured, persons killed. Model: Poisson GLM of monthly counts on group x month fixed effects ... specifically log E[count] = group + month(calendar) + group x post, on a 24-month window Aug 2021-Jul 2023, with Pearson-scaled (quasi-Poisson) standard errors. Event-study figure of the new/old ratio by month, Jan 2020 - Dec 2024, to show pre-trends. Placebo: fake start 1 Aug 2021 on Aug 2020-Jul 2022. Mechanism check: camera tickets ('PHTO SCHOOL ZN SPEED VIOLATION') by issue hour in Open Parking and Camera Violations (nc67-uf89) should appear in the new hours from Aug 2022. Design limits: citywide counts dilute a local effect; night and weekend travel recovered from the pandemic at a different pace from weekday daytime travel, which can bias the DiD in either direction; no exposure (vehicle-miles) by hour.
alternatives: Differential post-pandemic recovery of night and weekend traffic (nightlife) relative to weekday daytime
Changes in NYPD crash reporting or in the share of crashes with location and time recorded
E-bike and moped growth, concentrated in evening delivery hours
Regression to the mean if 2021-22 night crash levels were unusually high
